title: Build Harbor Relay Trivia & Scoreboard
summary: Build the game from one shared prompt. Score your first file with the same five checks as the other tools.
requires: You need access to the tool for the build, an empty practice folder, and a browser to play the saved file. For the fit check, use an iPad or an iPad-sized browser view and record which you used.
features: Claude can show an app in an Artifact. Claude Code can make the file in a folder.
roles: Use the same pretend mail report to check whether a double tap counts a row twice.
Give four helpers the same made-up team list. Check that each turn goes to the right team.
Build one small game four ways. Choose the one you enjoy playing and editing.
prompt: Build a single-file offline web app (`index.html`) for a two-team pass-and-play game called Harbor Relay. Use a clean, bright, high-contrast theme that works on both iPad and desktop screens. Include: (1) Team Blue and Team Gold starting at 0 points, (2) a deck of 6 built-in harbor trivia questions with 3 multiple-choice buttons each, (3) +2 points for a correct answer and 0 points for a wrong answer, automatically switching turns after each answer, (4) a visible Question X of 6 counter and a short explanation after each pick, (5) locking the answer buttons after a pick and after question 6 ends the game, and (6) a Play Again button that resets both scores to 0, resets to Team Blue, and returns to Question 1.

steps.title: Open Claude
steps.text: Go to claude.ai and start a new chat. If an Artifact opens beside the reply, that is where you can preview the game. For Claude Code, open an empty practice folder and start a new session there. Choose one route for this run.
steps.help: An Artifact is a thing Claude makes, such as an app. If your first reply offers only code, you can save that code as the game file.

steps.title: Send the shared prompt once
steps.text: Copy Your prompt from this page and send it by itself. Save the first reply before asking for any changes.
steps.help: Leave the five checks in the book. All four builders get just the words in the prompt.

steps.title: Keep the first file
steps.text: Open the Artifact beside the chat and use its download or code view. In Claude Code, look for index.html in your practice folder. If you get an HTML code block, copy its contents into a plain-text file named index.html.
steps.help: Leave out the code fence marks. Keep the file just as it came back. If there is no usable HTML, record what you received.

steps.title: Play the original with the network off
steps.text: Save index.html by itself in an empty folder. Turn off Wi-Fi or unplug the network. Open the saved file in a browser that runs local HTML. Check the starting team, both scores and each of the six question numbers. Read the short explanation after every pick.
steps.help: A chat preview may work online even when the file needs the internet. Test the saved file in a fresh browser window. For iPad fit, use the same browser and screen size for all four games.

steps.title: Test both teams and the lock
steps.text: In one game, have Blue get all three turns right and Gold miss all three. On the first right answer, tap the same choice twice quickly. Look for Blue 2, Gold 0 and just one turn passed. Finish all six questions.
steps.help: Use the answers stored in the file or learn them in a practice round. Another game may ask different questions. Use the same pattern of right and wrong picks.

steps.title: Test a win, a tie and a clean replay
steps.text: The first game should end Blue 6, Gold 0. Try another answer after the end. Press Play Again and check the first turn, scores and question number. Play again with six right answers. The tie should be 6 to 6.
steps.help: On each question count the three choices. After each pick, try tapping before moving on. A score or question that changes twice is a failed lock.

steps.title: Record the first try before making an edit
steps.text: Use the five checks on this page. Give one point for each pass. Open the four-tool scorecard to record what you saw. Once you have scored the originals, use the same follow-up there for each tool.
steps.help: Keep a copy of the first file. If you have only tested one tool, leave the other scorecards blank.

check: Layout & Mobile Fit: All buttons and text fit cleanly on an iPad screen without overlapping or sideways scrolling.
Scoring & Turn Switch: Correct answers add +2 to the active team only; wrong answers add 0; turns alternate Blue -> Gold after every question.
Click-Lock Guard: Tapping an answer twice on the same question cannot award +4 points or skip a turn.
Game End & Winner: After Question 6, answer buttons lock and a clear winner (or tie) banner appears.
Clean Replay: Play Again resets both scores to 0, sets Question 1 of 6, and returns the first turn to Team Blue.

Win earns 1, tie and loss earn 0.

steps.title: Set up the practice space
steps.text: Open Claude Code on a computer. Select a new, empty practice folder for this lab.
steps.help: The selected folder should be empty. In Finder or File Explorer, make a folder named claude-code-16 if you need one.

steps.title: Build the app
steps.text: Paste the prompt into the project chat. After it writes index.html, open that file in a browser.
steps.help: Look for the controls named in the prompt. If a control is missing, name it in the same chat and ask the helper to add it.

steps.title: Play the first round
steps.text: Pick Paper for all three rounds. Read both moves each time and write down the result.
steps.help: The results are win, tie and loss in order. Final score is 1 of 3.

steps.title: Try a change
steps.text: Press Replay. Pick Paper, Scissors, Rock. Try one more press after round three.
steps.help: If Paper loses to Rock, check the pair from the player's point of view. Test all three winning pairs.

check: The results are win, tie and loss in order. Final score is 1 of 3.
The score resets before the game. Three wins give 3 of 3. The extra press cannot change the result.

title: Catch the odd word
summary: Find the item that does not belong with the others. Give the answer a reason as well as a point.
requires: Open Claude Code on a computer. Select a new, empty practice folder for this lab.
features: Use Claude Code to write a local page. Try the page in your browser.
roles: Teach which sample field belongs in a mail report.
Make a training quiz with explanations.
Build a word game with replay.
prompt: Build one index.html file with its style and JavaScript inside. Show three word buttons per round. Accept one guess, explain the correct answer and show Next. End after three rounds. Keep score and add Replay. Use these practice values: Round 1: spoon, fork, mitten (mitten is clothing). Round 2: bus, apple, tram (apple is fruit). Round 3: drum, flute, map (map is a guide).

steps.title: Set up the practice space
steps.text: Open Claude Code on a computer. Select a new, empty practice folder for this lab.
steps.help: The selected folder should be empty. In Finder or File Explorer, make a folder named claude-code-17 if you need one.

steps.title: Build the app
steps.text: Paste the prompt into the project chat. After it writes index.html, open that file in a browser.
steps.help: Look for the controls named in the prompt. If a control is missing, name it in the same chat and ask the helper to add it.

steps.title: Play the first round
steps.text: Choose mitten, apple and drum. Try to change the last guess after the explanation appears.
steps.help: The first two are right. The third answer is map. Final score stays at 2 of 3.

steps.title: Try a change
steps.text: Replay and choose all three correct words. Read the last explanation before closing the game.
steps.help: If the last explanation mentions clothing, look up the reason on the current round's card.

check: The first two are right. The third answer is map. Final score stays at 2 of 3.
The second score is 3 of 3. Each round gives its own reason.

Save the three codes in this browser's storage. Try to read saved codes on open. If saving is blocked, show a message and let the page still work. title: Build a one-button lunch poll
summary: Give each practice ballot one vote. See how a tie looks before declaring a winner.

features: Use Claude Code to write a local page. Try the page in your browser.
roles: Count answers to a pretend mail survey.
Compare votes in a sample team poll.
Build a poll with a fair tie rule.
prompt: Build one index.html file with its style and JavaScript inside. Build a poll with a ballot ID box, three choices and Vote. One ID may vote once. Show all three totals and announce a tie when the highest positive totals match. Show No votes at the start. Add Reset poll. Use these practice values: Choices are Soup, Wrap and Salad. Practice ballot IDs are T1, T2 and T3.

title: Make a mailbox size dial
summary: Show how full a pretend mailbox is. Include a message for a missing size or an impossible limit.
requires: Open Claude Code on a computer. Select a new, empty practice folder for this lab.
features: Use Claude Code to write a local page. Try the page in your browser.
roles: Check practice mailbox usage.
Show how close a team list is to its limit.
Build an easy-to-read progress dial.
prompt: Build one index.html file with its style and JavaScript inside. Make a small size reader. Add boxes for used and limit, a Check button, a bar and a printed percentage. Warn at 90 percent and above. Call an empty value or a limit of zero Needs review. Reject negative sizes. Use these practice values: Used 25, limit 100. Other test pairs are 0 and 100, 90 and 100, 5 and 0. Print OK below 90 percent and Warning from 90 percent up when the inputs are valid.

steps.help: The pairs give 25 percent OK and 0 percent OK. Zero is a valid size.

steps.title: Try a change
steps.text: Try 90 and 100, then 5 and 0. Set the limit back to 100 before you empty Used. Check each label.
steps.help: If the screen shows Infinity, check the limit before dividing. If zero used disappears, check for a blank string first.

If a checkbox changes after finishing, clear the finish state. Add Start again. Use these practice values: Steps: Read sample, Check total, Save note.

title: Build a sliding tile game
summary: Move nearby number tiles into one empty space. Work a one-move puzzle and try a trick move.

Build a training exercise with valid step order.
Make a sliding puzzle with a win state.
prompt: Build one index.html file with its style and JavaScript inside. Make four large grid buttons. A tile can move only if it shares a side with the empty square. Count legal moves. On the solved board announce a win and freeze moves. Reset returns to the starting layout. Use these practice values: Use a two-by-two board. Start [1,2,empty,3]. The goal is [1,2,3,empty].

steps.text: At the start click tile 2 diagonally across from empty. Then click tile 3. Read the board and move count.
steps.help: The diagonal click changes nothing. Tile 3 slides left. The solved board shows one move.

steps.title: Try a change
steps.text: Reset. Click tile 1, then tile 1 again to bring it back. Finish with tile 3.
steps.help: If tile 2 moves on the first click, compare the row and column distances. Their sum should be one.

title: Build a rate chart with an honest scale
summary: Compare two toy plans. Find the point where the cheaper plan changes as use grows.
requires: Open Claude Code on a computer. Select a new, empty practice folder for this lab.
features: Use Claude Code to write a local page. Try the page in your browser.
roles: Compare fake per-mailbox report costs.
Estimate two ways to handle a team task.
Build a tool for comparing two plans.
prompt: Build one index.html file with its style and JavaScript inside. Make a chart and a number box for whole uses. Print both totals beside their bars and mark the cheaper plan or Tie. Both bars must use the same scale. Reject negative or fractional use counts. Use these practice values: Plan A costs 2 coins for each use. Plan B costs 5 coins plus 1 coin per use. Try 0, 4, 5 and 6 uses.

steps.title: Try the sample
steps.text: Set uses to 4, then 5, then 6. Compare the labels and the bars.
steps.help: At 4, A costs 8 and B costs 9. At 5 they tie at 10. At 6, B costs 11 and A costs 12.

steps.title: Try a change
steps.text: Try 0 and then -1. Look at both the result and the error area.
steps.help: If both bars look full at 4, give them a shared maximum. Check the printed numbers even when the picture looks right.

writeYourOwn.compare: Did you tell the helper what identifies a file and when to stop before reporting?

title: Make a puzzle clock without real waiting
summary: Run two timed puzzle rounds. A manual clock makes pause, resume and scoring easy to test.

Build a timed training activity.
Ship a two-round timed game.
prompt: Build one index.html file with its style and JavaScript inside. Build a two-round clock game with Start, Tick, Pause, Solve and Replay. While running, Tick uses one tick and Solve finishes the round with points. Running out of ticks ends that round with zero. Next round resets ticks. After two rounds show the final score. Freeze actions while paused or finished. Use these practice values: Round one lasts 3 ticks. Solve button earns 2 points. Round two also lasts 3 ticks.

title: Capstone · Build an offline shift handoff
summary: Read a fake mailbox list, mark rows reviewed, then save and restore the handoff. A classmate should be able to check the whole trip.

features: Use Claude Code to write a local page. Try the page in your browser.
roles: Build a read-only review desk for fake mail data.
Hand off a checked team list offline.
Ship a portable app with backup and restore.
prompt: Build one index.html file with its style and JavaScript inside. Build a local handoff app in one HTML file. Show all rows and queue counts. Say Missing for a blank and print 0 for zero. Allow a reader to mark rows reviewed. Show reviewed count and known queue total. Add Export JSON and Import JSON from a chosen local file. Validate version, row IDs, counts and review flags before replacing any saved rows. Add Restore sample. Include a button to run saved example checks. No server or account is needed to run the finished page. Use these practice values: Rows: M1 Queue=4, M2 Queue=0, M3 Queue empty. Checked status starts false for each.

steps.title: Set up the practice space

steps.title: Try a change
steps.text: Try a file with version 99, then one with M1 listed twice. Reopen the HTML while the network is off, load the good export again and run its checks.
steps.help: If a failed import wipes the list, read the new file into a temporary list. Replace the old list only after every row passes.

check: The restored handoff says 2 of 3 reviewed and 4 known items. M2 keeps 0, M3 says Missing. The review flags survive the trip.
Both bad files give errors and leave the current handoff untouched. Offline, the good export still restores the same three rows and both totals.
